questions.q: When the CHK-108 PR is opened against main, which CI workflow runs?
options: Both product-catalog-ci.yml and checkout-ci.yml
Only checkout-ci.yml, because the change falls under services/checkout/** and path filters scope each workflow
Only product-catalog-ci.yml, since it runs on every PR regardless of path
Neither — a maintainer must trigger CI manually for ticket-based changes
questions.explain: Each service's workflow is scoped with a path filter. Since CHK-108 only touches `services/checkout/`, only `checkout-ci.yml` triggers; `product-catalog-ci.yml`'s filter doesn't match.

questions.q: What two conditions must both be true before the CHK-108 PR can be squash-merged into main?
options: The PR must be open for at least 24 hours and have a linked ticket
At least 1 reviewer approval and passing CI, enforced as branch protection rules on main
A maintainer must manually disable branch protection first
The image must already be deployed to production
questions.explain: main's branch protection rules require 1 reviewer approval and green CI before a PR can merge — both are satisfied before the squash merge in this walkthrough.

questions.q: What happens automatically the moment the CHK-108 merge lands on main, with no human action required?
options: The change deploys straight to northbridge-prod
A semver tag is cut automatically
The deploy-dev job runs: OIDC login, AKS context set to the dev cluster, and helm upgrade --install to northbridge-dev tagged with the merge SHA
Nothing — a maintainer must manually trigger the dev deploy
questions.explain: Lesson 11's deploy-dev job is gated to run automatically on any merge to main, deploying the SHA-tagged image straight to the northbridge-dev namespace.

questions.q: After the maintainer pushes tag v1.5.0, what is the ONE place in the entire walkthrough where a human approval is required?
options: Before the PR can even be opened
Before CI is allowed to run on the PR
Before the deploy-staging job runs
Before the deploy-prod job is allowed to run, because it's tied to the "production" GitHub Environment's protection rule
questions.explain: Staging deploys automatically on the tag push with no approval needed. The only required human-in-the-loop moment is the pending deployment pause on the production Environment before deploy-prod runs.

questions.q: According to this lesson, what does Phase 4 (the next chapter) cover that this lesson only foreshadows?
options: A second cloud provider added for redundancy
The monitoring that would have caught the flash-sale checkout latency incident, and the full story of the PaymentPro secrets near-miss first mentioned in Lesson 10
A rewrite of checkout from Python to Node.js
Switching from Helm to raw kubectl manifests
questions.explain: This lesson explicitly points ahead to Phase 4 (monitoring/alerting and security scanning), which covers both the flash-sale latency incident and the full PaymentPro near-miss worked example.
